original_assignment_row.title: Refugee Admissions and Asylum Elimination - Complete Protection System Termination
original_assignment_row.description_short: Refugee Admissions and Asylum Elimination - Complete Protection System Termination
original_assignment_row.description_medium: Trump’s January 2025 order suspended entry under the U.S. Refugee Admissions Program starting January 27, pending a review of whether the program should resume. It also paused decisions on refugee applications, while allowing case-by-case admissions when officials found entry to be in the national interest. The order called for an initial report within 90 days and further reports every 90 days.
original_assignment_row.description_long: Donald Trump terminated the United States Refugee Admissions Program and eliminated asylum pathways by suspending all refugee processing, ending Temporary Protected Status for 850,000 individuals, and eliminating T and U visas for victims of human trafficking and violent crimes while consolidating immigration agencies into single enforcement entity without humanitarian functions. The comprehensive protection elimination represented Trump's implementation of Project 2025's plan to 'slash immigration levels' by removing all pathways for vulnerable individuals to seek safety in the United States, effectively ending America's historic role as refuge for people fleeing persecution, violence, and humanitarian disasters. The systematic asylum destruction included directing USCIS to cease application intake for asylum, TPS, and victim visas whenever backlogs were deemed 'excessive,' creating deliberate administrative barriers that prevented eligible individuals from accessing legal protections while forcing them into undocumented status vulnerable to deportation. Trump's refugee program termination violated international humanitarian law obligations by ending protections for individuals fleeing 'armed conflicts or environmental disasters' while eliminating work authorization that had allowed protected individuals to rebuild lives and contribute economically to American communities. The protection system elimination consolidated key immigration agencies into single powerful entity that 'stripped oversight and accountability from ICE' while removing humanitarian considerations from immigration decisions, transforming what had been 'fair immigration system into one driven by enforcement and exclusion' rather than protection of vulnerable populations. The refugee and asylum termination represented what human rights organizations called abandonment of American values and international obligations, ending decades of humanitarian leadership while forcing vulnerable individuals back to countries where they faced persecution, violence, or death due to conditions beyond their control.

It says Hopkins brought up to $200,000 in cash to a closing attended by Trump and that a limo delivered the money to a bank. Hahn clarified the next day that he had overstated the evidence and should have described a relative risk reduction. original_assignment_row.description_long: The FDA authorized emergency use of convalescent plasma for COVID-19 on August 23, 2020. At a White House briefing, Commissioner Stephen Hahn described the evidence as showing a “35% improvement in survival,” while Trump praised the authorization as a major achievement. The supplied account says the announcement followed Trump’s public criticism of the FDA the previous day over delays in treatment. That timing can explain why the episode raised questions about political pressure, but it does not show that Hahn made the statement at Trump’s direction or knowingly misrepresented the evidence. The next day, Hahn said criticism of his remarks was justified and clarified that the data showed a relative risk reduction, not an absolute reduction. Convalescent plasma uses antibodies from donated blood; an emergency-use authorization is a regulatory decision, not proof of a newly discovered treatment.
